task_instruction: Review the attached file (tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/review_target.py) for Clean Architecture and SOLID violations, per this repo's rules/coding-standards.md. For each violation: cite the file:line, name the specific principle violated, state its severity, and suggest a fix. Do not fix the code yourself -- produce a review report only.
completion_threshold_rationale: RETROSPECTIVE, not pre-registered -- stated honestly (an earlier draft of this field wrongly claimed 'pre-registered alongside the rubric, before any run'; that claim was false and is corrected here). The task's 10 review_small_diff runs (docs/bench-agent-cost/20260905/{raw,scored}/) were already committed to main by PR #121 before this field was added by PR #122; the threshold was therefore chosen with full visibility of the resulting quality scores (7-10 out of 10 across all runs), which is the opposite of the Fisher-style blind pre-registration this benchmark's design doc otherwise requires. The chosen value (5/10: magic_number 2pts + srp_mixed_io_logic 3pts, summed against the rubric's total-points gate the code actually implements -- see analyze_results.py's quality_score/report_completion_gated_tokens) sits with real margin under the observed minimum of 7, and the resulting measurement (100%/100% completion, no differentiation) is the least favorable outcome for arguing this metric matters -- so this is not tuned toward a desired result -- but neither fact makes 'pre-registered' an honest label for it. Rule for every future task: `completion_threshold_points` must be fixed before that task's first run, committed in the same change that introduces the task, and never edited after any run exists for it. This task is the one documented exception, corrected here rather than left mislabeled.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the unnamed/unsourced discount threshold (500) and multiplier (0.9) as a magic-number violation (coding-standards.md §3.1).
Identifies that process_order mixes I/O (DB read, HTTP call) with business logic (discount calculation) in one function -- an SRP/layering violation (§1.1, §3.1).
Identifies the silent `return None` on a non-200 payment response as an unnamed failure mode / swallowed error (§9 anti-pattern list).
Every reported finding cites a specific file:line, not just a general description.
Severity assigned is proportional to consequence (the SRP/payment-flow issues are ranked at or above the magic number, not flooded with equal-weight style nits).
Reports no violation that is not actually present in the fixture (no false positives).
